Page64 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version 4.5 GENERAL SITE ARRANGEMENT Pre-FEED layout activities initially focused on gathering inputs to design basis and obtaining lessons learned through review of similar projects carried out by Entr. As the PFD and MEL developed, the site layout was defined accordingly and included in a 3D model utilizing Aveva E3D version 3.1 with overviews provided in Navisworks 2018 along with overlays within Google Earth. The following sections will provide some additional details to each area of the site and parameters or logic used to help develop the layout. 4.5.1 OVERVIEW The site location for the Tampa Regional Intermodal CO Hub (T-RICH) is on Pendola Point within the 2 boundaries of Port Tampa Bay as previously shown in Figs. 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3. Preliminary PFD's and MEL were developed to help determine process and equipment size requirements. This information along with other similar historical projects were utilized to start the development of a site layout while investigating multiple potential layout options suited for the site. Based on extensive discussions and feedback from process, mechanical, safety, electrical, construction, and client updates, it has been recommended to design a facility that minimizes the use of available real estate while providing ample provisions for safety, efficient process operations, maintenance, and construction requirements. The recommended option for this project phase is a facility incorporating 11 large horizontal pressure vessels (10 meters in diameter and 32.3 meters in length) with two 50% compression / liquefaction trains supplied with CO via pipeline, rail, and truck. An overview of the site 2 layout can be seen in Fig. 4.12, with closeups of certain areas in later figures. The remainder of Section 4.5 will provide further details around the options and logic used to help develop the current site arrangement and identify additional work to be carried out during the FEED phase. There are many factors which have to be taken into consideration when laying out a CO receiving, 2 compression, liquefaction, storage, and export facility. Safety considerations for construction and operating personnel, adjacent populated areas and facilities are of top priority. Finding a balance to satisfy not only safety, but construction and operational activities while being economically viable for the client and with minimal environmental impact is of great importance and is the end goal to have a successful project. It has been determined during the Pre-FEED phase that such a layout can be achieved based on available data received to date. Subsequent phases of the project (FEED, Detail Design) will help further refine the design and data to ensure viability of the project.
